findings.title: Missing Zero Address Validation in Constructor
findings.description: The constructor does not validate that `_token0`, `_token1`, `_factory`, or blast-related addresses are not zero addresses. This could lead to locked funds or unexpected behavior if zero addresses are passed.
findings.location: constructor(address, address, address, address, address, address)

findings.title: No Duplicate Token Validation
findings.description: The constructor does not check if `token0 == token1`. Deploying with identical token addresses would cause incorrect fee distribution and potential loss of funds.
findings.location: constructor(address, address, address, address, address, address)

findings.title: Potential Reentrancy in claimFeesFor
findings.description: The `claimFeesFor` function performs two external token transfers without a reentrancy guard. If the recipient or token contracts are malicious (e.g., ERC777 with callbacks), state could be manipulated between transfers. While limited by the `msg.sender == pair` check, compromised pair contracts could exploit this.

findings.title: Incomplete Access Control Implementation
findings.description: The `_checkAccessForManageBlastERC20Rebasing` function is truncated/incomplete. The implementation is cut off mid-function, making it impossible to verify proper access control for Blast rebasing operations.

findings.title: Unchecked Return Data in _safeTransfer
findings.description: While the implementation checks for empty data or boolean return, some non-compliant ERC20 tokens may behave unexpectedly. The pattern is generally acceptable but should be documented.

findings.title: Centralized Fee Claiming via Pair Contract
findings.description: All fee claims must go through the pair contract (`msg.sender == pair`). If the pair contract is upgradeable or has vulnerabilities, the entire fee distribution mechanism could be compromised.

findings.title: Missing Function Implementations
findings.description: The provided code snippet only shows interface definitions and partial library implementations. The actual RouterV2 contract logic is missing, preventing a complete security analysis.

findings.title: Incomplete Math.sqrt() Implementation
findings.description: The Math.sqrt() function appears to be cut off mid-implementation. If this function is incomplete or incorrectly implemented, it could lead to inaccurate calculations for liquidity operations.

findings.title: Potential Interface Inconsistencies
findings.description: The IBaseV1Pair interface includes a non-standard function signature: getAmountOut(uint, address) that differs from typical Uniswap/Solidly implementations. This could indicate customization but also potential compatibility issues.
